findings.text: A node type is classified as dense when it orders below the leaf threshold. Dense handling counts occupancy directly while other leaf types use pivot intervals.

Leaf maximum free extent is derived from slot occupancy and pivot bounds. Dense leaves count the longest run of empty slots. Other leaves treat an empty first slot and an empty trailing slot at the address space maximum as edge extents, otherwise measure pivot differences at empty slots and assume empty slots never occur adjacently.

Gap bookkeeping propagates upward only through range nodes that carry gaps. A changed child extent updates the parent gap entry, then either retains or moves the cached maximum offset, recomputing by scan when the previous maximum shrinks, and continues toward the root.
Node metadata carries a gap selector offset and an end offset. Both are written together during initialization and cleared together when a destroyed non-leaf node has no surviving child metadata.

Root store distinguishes clearing, expansion, and direct installation. A null entry with zero start clears the root. A non trivial range or a specially encoded entry expands into a new leaf root. Otherwise the entry is installed directly and the walk state returns to start.

Root expansion builds a single leaf root of height one. It preserves any prior root content, places supplied start and end boundaries into pivots with a terminal maximum pivot when needed, records parent linkage to the tree, initializes metadata, and publishes the new root.
Tree height lives in a masked flag field with defined mask, shift, and maximum. Update preserves other flag bits and validates against the maximum.

Pointer encodings use dedicated low-bit tags for root nodes, root parents, internal parent links, and topiary linkage. Parent link construction combines the parent address with slot and type fields after clearing tag bits.

Write protection is tested through an external-lock or internal-lock predicate. Root and slot reads are performed under that predicate, so callers must hold the appropriate write lock when invoking locked root or slot access.
Tree mutation helpers that publish replacement nodes and scan for not-yet-adopted children require the tree lock to be held by the caller.
Node allocation first reuses a state-carried spare node when present, otherwise allocates from a sheaf-backed cache, and always returns zeroed storage.
Full-range replacement moves from any prior root to either an empty tree of height zero or a new one-entry leaf root of height one, then walks and discards the prior root subtree when it was a node.

Destruction descends to leaves while marking visited nodes dead, saving their types and back links. Leaf children are detached in order until an absent child is found. Interior traversal then iterates remaining siblings. Memory is either freed immediately in bulk or left for deferred reclamation with metadata cleared, depending on RCU mode.

A store spanning nodes uses duplicated left and right walk states positioned at the range ends. Full-range stores reduce to root replacement. Null stores may extend across adjacent empty space. Otherwise data from both sides is combined level by level and ascended until complete, followed by publication and range repositioning.

Replacement publication installs the new nodes, marks the old entry dead, adopts child back pointers in bounded breadth-first groups, collects wholly replaced old subtrees separately from partially retained paths, and reclaims all discarded nodes with RCU-aware freeing. Allocation-mode trees also refresh the known gap after replacement.

Adoption rewrites back pointers for the occupied child prefix of a new internal node. Each child receives the parent address combined with its slot index and internal type, and only range-like parent types are accepted.

Node death is made visible with an ordering barrier before readers can observe replacement. Freed nodes use deferred reclamation, and freeing asserts the node was already marked dead through self linkage.
Two helpers have external linkage in these fragments: the leaf-detachment scan used during destruction and the parent-slot assignment routine used during adoption.
The test assertion macro counts every evaluation as a run and counts only successful evaluations as passed, logging function, line, and pass state on failure.
